To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

MIB 1, MIB 2 and MIB 1 are true Ki‐ 67 equivalents, that they label proliferating cells in fresh and formalin‐fixed, microwave‐processed parafin sections, and that they are useful tools for the assessment of cell proliferation.
monoclonal antibodies MIB 1, MIB 2, and MIB 4 recognize the Ki‐67‐associated antigen, which is detectable in microwave‐processed, formalin‐fixed, and paraffin‐ embedded tissues.
microwave‐processed formaldehyde‐fixed, paraf in‐ embedded sections are a reliable source of material for immunohistochemical detection of Ki‐ 67 antigen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new antibodies for the assessment of cell proliferation.
the development of a new method for immunohistochemical detection of cell proliferation.
the detection of proliferative activity by means of the Ki‐ 67 antigen in formalin‐fixed, microwave‐processed, paraffin sections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MIB 1 is the most suitable marker for the detection of proliferating cells in routinely processed paraffin‐sectioned tissue.
the Ki‐67 antibody is not suitable for the detection of proliferating cells in formalin‐fixed, routinely processed paraffin tissue sections.

the MIB 1 antibody is a reliable and sensitive marker for the detection of cells in all active phases of the cell cycle, which can be used routinely in paraffin‐processed sections of formalin or alcohol‐fixed tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ki‐67‐reactive MIB antibodies are useful tools for the detection of cell proliferation in formalin‐fixed, microwave‐processed parafﬁn sections.
the Ki‐67 antibody can be used on microwave‐processed formaldehyde‐fixed paraff in sections of routinely processed material.
Ki‐67 antigen can be detected in formalin‐fixed and paraffin‐processed tissue sections after a short treatment in a microwave oven.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Ki‐67‐like monoclonal antibodies MIB 1, 2 and 3, when applied to formalin‐fixed, microwave‐processed parafin sections, are a valuable tool to study the cell kinetics of normal and neoplastically transformed cells.
the MIB 1 antibody can be used on archival paraffin‐fixed, microwave‐processed material to detect the Ki‐67‐positive cell population.
the use of microwave processing of paraffin sections allows for the detection of Ki67 antigen on formalin‐fixed, archival paraffin material.
